units.sourceHTML: 8 Merging From a Common Ancestor

units.text: When two people have made changes to copies of the same file, ⟦0⟧ can produce a merged output that contains both sets of changes together with warnings about conflicts.
units.sourceHTML: When two people have made changes to copies of the same file, diff3 can produce a merged output that contains both sets of changes together with warnings about conflicts.

units.text: One might imagine programs with names like ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ to compare more than three files simultaneously, but in practice the need rarely arises. You can use ⟦2⟧ to merge three or more sets of changes to a file by merging two change sets at a time.
units.sourceHTML: One might imagine programs with names like diff4 and diff5 to compare more than three files simultaneously, but in practice the need rarely arises. You can use diff3 to merge three or more sets of changes to a file by merging two change sets at a time.

units.text: ⟦0⟧ can incorporate changes from two modified versions into a common preceding version. This lets you merge the sets of changes represented by the two newer files. units.text: You can think of this as subtracting ⟦0⟧ from ⟦1⟧ and adding the result to ⟦2⟧, or as merging into ⟦3⟧ the changes that would turn ⟦4⟧ into ⟦5⟧. This merging is well-defined as long as ⟦6⟧ and ⟦7⟧ match in the neighborhood of each such change. This fails to be true when all three input files differ or when only ⟦8⟧ differs; we call this a ⟦9⟧conflict⟦10⟧. When all three input files differ, we call the conflict an ⟦11⟧overlap⟦12⟧.
units.sourceHTML: You can think of this as subtracting older from yours and adding the result to mine, or as merging into mine the changes that would turn older into yours. This merging is well-defined as long as mine and older match in the neighborhood of each such change. This fails to be true when all three input files differ or when only older differs; we call this a conflict. When all three input files differ, we call the conflict an overlap.

units.text: ⟦0⟧ gives you several ways to handle overlaps and conflicts. You can omit overlaps or conflicts, or select only overlaps, or mark conflicts with special ‘⟦1⟧’ and ‘⟦2⟧’ lines.
units.sourceHTML: diff3 gives you several ways to handle overlaps and conflicts. You can omit overlaps or conflicts, or select only overlaps, or mark conflicts with special ‘<<<<<<<’ and ‘>>>>>>>’ lines.

units.text: ⟦0⟧ can output the merge results as an ⟦1⟧ script that that can be applied to the first file to yield the merged output. However, it is usually better to have ⟦2⟧ generate the merged output directly; this bypasses some problems with ⟦3⟧.
units.sourceHTML: diff3 can output the merge results as an ed script that that can be applied to the first file to yield the merged output. However, it is usually better to have diff3 generate the merged output directly; this bypasses some problems with ed.
